# Time till' AI — full reference for agents

Time till' AI is a provider quota-window tracker for AI coding harnesses, by True-Line AI LLC (https://timetillai.app, https://true-line.github.io/time-till-ai/).

It is a static page with no backend: all state lives in the visitor's browser (IndexedDB), derived from timestamps, so timers survive tab closure and clock-real restarts. Agents integrate by opening hash-links. Nothing authenticates, nothing writes to GitHub, and opening a link is equivalent to a human clicking in the app.

## State model

Each provider is always in exactly one state:

- `open` — a quota window is running; countdown to reset (brand-colored ring).
- `capped` — the provider reported the limit was hit; counting down to recovery (red ring).
- `cooldown` — token pool exhausted; locked until cooldown ends (red ring).
- `fresh` — reset happened within the last 90 minutes; full capacity.
- `ready` — idle; no window armed (or token pool has remaining tokens).

For token-pool providers the ring shows tokens left (green > 40%, amber > 15%, red below).

## Quota kinds per provider

- `rolling` — window starts when armed (first message), lasts N hours (default 5). Reset = armed + N h.
- `weekly` — calendar quota; the period runs Monday 00:00 local → next Monday 00:00.
- `tokens` — token pool with cooldown: once `pool` tokens are consumed, none are available for `cooldownH` hours (e.g. Qwen Code free tier: 1M tokens, 24h lock).

## Deep-link protocol

Links are the app URL plus a hash. Base examples: `https://timetillai.app/` (custom domain) or `https://true-line.github.io/time-till-ai/` (Pages). Open links with `open` (macOS), `xdg-open` (Linux), `start` (Windows), or any browser/webview.

### Actions

- `#start=<provider-id>` — arm the provider's quota window now (rolling: `hours` long; weekly: current Monday→Monday period). Ignored if a window is already active.
- `#cap=<provider-id>` — mark the provider capped (limit hit). If no window was armed, one is reconstructed from the reset time (e.g. a 5h provider capped until 22:44 shows started 17:44). Without `resets`/`in` and no active window it is ignored. For token providers this drains the pool instead.
- `#drain=<provider-id>` — mark a token pool exhausted; starts its cooldown. Ignored if a cooldown is already running.

### Parameters (combine with `&`)

- `&resets=HH:MM` — with `#cap`: absolute reset time, e.g. copied verbatim from the provider CLI's rate-limit message ("resets at 18:44"). Parsed as the next occurrence of that wall-clock time.
- `&in=<duration>` — relative duration instead: `38m`, `6h`, `2d`, `90s`. With `#cap`: recovery in that long. With `#start`: custom window length overriding the provider default.
- `&used=<n>` — with `#drain`: tokens consumed (e.g. `620k`, `1m`, `400000`). Defaults to the full pool.
- `&src=<agent-name>` — provenance tag for who opened the link (e.g. `zcode`, `codex`, `claude`). Stored with the window record.

### Semantics

- **Idempotent**: a link whose action is already satisfied (window active, cooldown running, provider unknown) is ignored with a toast — safe to call from recurring hooks.
- **One-shot**: the hash is applied on page load, then stripped from the address bar; reloads never re-fire it.
- **Explicit arming only**: windows never auto-rearm. If your harness sends its first message of a session, that is the moment to open `#start`.

## Provider roster (seed)

IDs are lowercase, used verbatim in links:

| id | provider | quota kind | spec docs |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude | Claude | 5h rolling | — |
| codex | Codex | 5h rolling | — |
| zcode | Z-Code | 5h rolling | — |
| qwen | Qwen Code | 1M tokens · 24h cooldown | https://docs.qwencloud.com/resources/free-quota |
| muse | Muse | 5h rolling | — |
| opencode | OpenCode | weekly | https://opencode.ai/docs/console/models/#free-models |
| gemini | Gemini CLI | 5h rolling | — |
| cursor | Cursor | 5h rolling | — |
| copilot | GitHub Copilot | 5h rolling | — |
| amp | Amp | 5h rolling | — |

Users add their own providers (URL → favicon branding) with any quota kind; their IDs appear in the app's per-provider menu under "Copy start/cap/exhaust link". When integrating a specific user's harness, prefer the roster block in the app's **Agent links** modal ("Copy instructions for agent") — it always reflects the live roster.

## Example wiring

Session-start hook (arm Z-Code whenever a coding session begins):

```json
"hooks": { "SessionStart": [{ "hooks": [{
  "type": "command",
  "command": "open 'https://timetillai.app/#start=zcode&src=zcode'"
}] }] }
```

Rate-limit handler (parse the reset time from the CLI message, then):

```
open 'https://timetillai.app/#cap=codex&resets=18:44&src=codex'
```

Free-tier exhaustion (after reading usage from the provider):

```
open 'https://timetillai.app/#drain=qwen&used=1m&src=qwen'
```

## Sync and data

- Cross-device sync: one JSON blob (`timetillai-state.json`) in a private GitHub gist. The gist ID is the shareable "session code" (read anywhere, even `curl`); a GitHub token on one device enables push. Last-write-wins by revision.
- Local backup: JSON export/import in Settings.
- The tab title always shows the next countdown, so a pinned tab is a live status surface.

## Operator

True-Line AI LLC — https://www.true-line.ai · app: https://timetillai.app · repo: https://github.com/true-line/time-till-ai

## Human-paste flow (no special UI needed)

When a human pastes a provider's rate-limit message into their AI chat — their coding agent, assistant, or harness — you (the agent) are the parser. Extract the provider and reset time from the message, then open the matching link. Example:

- Human pastes: "Usage limit reached (5.0). Your limit will reset at 6:44 PM."
- You resolve "6:44 PM" → `18:44`, match the provider (by name, domain, or context) to a roster id, and open:
  `<base>#cap=<provider-id>&resets=18:44&src=<your-name>`

If the message mentions token exhaustion rather than a time window, use `#drain=<provider-id>&used=<n>` instead. If no provider matches, say so — do not guess an id. Opening the link in the user's browser is the entire integration: no UI embedding, no API, no auth.

## Creating and updating providers via deep link (#add)

Provider ids in links can be any stable slug *you* choose — `#add` creates the provider on first use and updates only the fields the link provides afterwards. Same link twice = same result (idempotent). This lets an agent construct the full link chain before the provider exists.

```
#add=<slug>&name=DeepSeek%20v4.1%20Flash&url=qwen.ai&kind=tokens&pool=1m&cooldown=168h&expires=2026-12-13
#drain=<slug>&used=1m
#reset=<slug>              refill a token pool to full now (alias of the Reset pool action)
```

- `name=` display name (URL-encoded); derived from `url` if omitted
- `url=` / `domain=` provider domain for favicon branding (e.g. `qwen.ai`)
- `kind=` `rolling` (default) | `weekly` | `tokens`
- `hours=` rolling window length; `pool=` token pool size (`1m`, `500k`); `cooldown=` cooldown hours (`24h`, `168h`)
- `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` calendar expiry for free tiers that never refill — at expiry the pool shows `expired` and stops counting down
- `spec=` quota docs URL; `color=` hex accent

For per-model pools on one platform (e.g. two Qwen Cloud models with separate 1M pools), create one provider per model with distinct slugs — draining one never touches the other.

## Provenance and human-paste

`&src=<agent-name>` tags which agent fired a link. When a human pastes a rate-limit message into your chat, you are the parser: extract provider and reset time, then open `#cap=<id>&resets=HH:MM`. If no provider matches a message, create one with `#add` using a stable slug — do not drain a shared provider to avoid touching unrelated models.
